compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

observations.body: Aaron offers for himself and the people, blesses them, and fire from the LORD consumes the altar offering as the people shout and fall down.
observations.label: Fire answers the first priestly service

observations.body: The passage presents priestly service, blessing, glory, divine fire, joy, and prostration as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: priestly service, blessing, glory, divine fire, joy, and prostration

observations.body: The passage places inauguration beside priestly service, blessing, glory, divine fire, joy, and prostration.
observations.label: inauguration

payload.posture: Read Leviticus 9:1–24 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the extraordinary fire marks inauguration rather than the ordinary result of each sacrifice
payload.title: Fire answers the first priestly service
